About seven years, since 2019. I started as a junior web developer, moved through web developer and software engineer roles, and for the last three years I've been leading an AI team as a Solutions Architect.

NativeCamp is an online English platform for the Japanese market, with live lessons around the clock. I'm a Solutions Architect on it, and I contributed AI coaching and chat-support features and the real-time lesson infrastructure.

My day to day is TypeScript and Node on the backend, with Next.js, React or Vue on the front end, plus PHP and Laravel from earlier work. Data is PostgreSQL or MySQL, and I use Docker and CI/CD. For AI, it's Dify, n8n and the Claude, OpenAI and Gemini APIs.

I use Claude Code every day, and my team works spec-first with Spec Kit, so every feature starts from one clear plan. I review all AI-generated code before it ships. For products, I use tool calling and approved data so the AI stays accurate and safe.

I run daily stand-ups and code reviews, mentor the juniors, and keep everyone working from the same spec. I also flag technical risks early with a mitigation plan, so quality and timelines are protected.

Taking a vague business problem to an architecture, a prototype and then production. Leading a team with code reviews and mentoring. And building AI features that are safe to put in front of customers.

Leading the AI team from ideas to production chatbots and automation that significantly reduced manual work. At the same time, I resolved critical issues and delivered multiple features on NativeCamp as Solutions Architect.

Tubag AI is a chat agent for small businesses that take appointments. It answers only from the business's approved information, checks availability, books and reschedules, captures leads, and hands over to a human. It's currently paused while the Messenger integration waits on Meta's app review.
